result:
Both tests pass. Summary of the fix:

**Root cause**: `Sentinel` is an `enum.Enum` whose members' values are bare `object()` instances. `Enum.__reduce_ex__` pickles by reconstructing via `Sentinel(self._value_)` â€” value-based lookup. Since a fresh unpickled `object()` is never `==` to the original, `pickle.loads` raised `ValueError: <object object at ...> is not a valid Sentinel`. `copy`/`deepcopy` happened to work only because this Python (3.13) has `Enum.__copy__`/`__deepcopy__` shortcuts, but they'd hit the same failure via `__reduce_ex__` on Python versions lacking those (click supports 3.10+).

**Fix** (`src/click/_utils.py`): overrode `Sentinel.__reduce_ex__` to reconstruct by name via `getattr(self.__class__, self._name_)` instead of by value, so all three operations return the original singleton correctly across Python versions.

Also added a regression test (`tests/test_utils/test_sentinel.py`) and a changelog entry.
